title: A late worker returns with a verdict
description: Worker A pauses long enough to lose its submission lease. Worker B takes a new lease and finishes judging. A resumes with an old verdict and tries to write it. How should the system keep this at-least-once execution from changing the final verdict or counting the submission twice?

options.text: Let whichever worker writes last replace the verdict and add another leaderboard update.
options.explanation: Wall-clock arrival order does not establish ownership. A stale worker could overwrite valid state or double-apply scoring.

options.text: Disable lease expiry so the first worker keeps the job even if it never returns.
options.explanation: That strands work on failed hosts and removes the recovery benefit of leased jobs.

options.text: Treat the queue as exactly once and omit checks at the verdict database.
options.explanation: A lease timeout can create duplicate execution. The database must defend the final write even when queue delivery is retried.

options.text: Fence verdict writes with the current lease or attempt token, reject A's stale write, and apply scoring idempotently per logical submission.
options.explanation: The current owner alone can finalize the submission. Duplicate execution is acceptable when conditional persistence and idempotent downstream updates prevent duplicate effects.
